notes: The adaptor targets the Flutterwave v4 API (unprefixed /customers, /payment-methods, /charges; OAuth access token sent as Bearer), not v3. Flutterwave publishes a machine spec only for v3 (/api/v3/openapi.json, every path under /v3/), so that was rejected as the wrong version; no v4 spec is public. This OpenAPI 3.0.3 was generated by mechanically parsing the 57 v4 endpoint sections of the vendor's llms-full.txt export (the same structured data the v4 reference pages render), so every documented v4 endpoint is present: 39 paths / 57 operations across customers, charges, orchestrator charges/orders/transfers, orders, payment methods, refunds, chargebacks, settlements, transfers, transfer recipients/senders/rates, virtual accounts, wallets, banks, mobile networks, fees and webhook resend; the refund.completed webhook payload is a component schema. Caveats: (1) the two DELETE operations document no success response, so 204 is assumed; (2) the docs show only the sandbox host (developersandbox-api.flutterwave.com); the production host f4bexperience.flutterwave.com comes from the vendor's earlier Environments page and answers like the sandbox gateway (401 JSON) but is not shown in the current reference; (3) the previous stub listed api.flutterwave.cloud/{developersandbox,f4bexternal} servers, which now time out, and note the adaptor builds URLs with new URL('/path', baseUrl), which drops any path prefix on baseUrl; (4) doc example values (names, emails, phones) were deliberately not copied as examples. Known generator defects (2026-11-13): (5) the parser marked each oneOf variant's discriminator with `default` instead of `enum`, so variants such as next_action's redirect_url / requires_pin overlapped and oneOf could never match; fixed in place by adding `enum: [<default>]` to the 50 discriminators (no other change). (6) Fixed 2026-11-16: 48 oneOf variants in six places (PaymentMethod, CreatePaymentMethodRequest, Charge.payment_method_details, Order.payment_method_details and the payment_method of the two orchestrator requests) had lost their property names and were allOf[string, string, object, ...], which no value can satisfy. Re-fetching llms-full.txt showed the cause is upstream: the v4 reference renders each 'Option N all of' with only the shared fields (request: type, customer_id, meta; response: id, type, customer_id, meta, device_fingerprint, client_ip, created_datetime) and omits the type-specific half, so the variant names are not in the reference at all. The schemas were rebuilt from those shared fields plus the request/response examples in the vendor's v4 guides (card, mobile-money, opay, ng-bank-account, ussd, pay-with-bank-transfer): a `type` discriminator plus the type-named object (`card`, `mobile_money`, `opay`, `bank_account`, `ussd`; `bank_transfer` in responses only). The reference counts 7 request and 9 response variants, so each oneOf ends with an 'other' variant (any other `type`, shared fields only) rather than inventing the undocumented ones. customer_id, device_fingerprint and client_ip are nullable in responses because the guide examples show null; fields shown only as null carry no type. The four embedded copies now $ref PaymentMethod / CreatePaymentMethodRequest. Create answers 201 per the reference (some guides label the same example '200 OK'). Still open: (7) the oneOf variants of CreateTransferRecipientRequest, CreateTransferSenderRequest, ResolveBankAccountRequest and CreateOrchestratorTransferRequest.payment_instruction are told apart in the docs only by `default` values (e.g. type bank_ngn, destination_currency NGN) that sit inside allOf members and were not turned into enums, so a body can match several variants and fail oneOf; not changed here because the docs give two different defaults for `type` in the same option and do not say which one discriminates.
